newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-GIAMBI HOMER IN NINTH LIFTS A'S PAST ORIOLES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-GIAMBI HOMER IN NINTH LIFTS A'S PAST ORIOLES.

text.p: Jason Giambi's smacked a two-run homer off reliever Randy Myers with two outs in the ninth inning to lift the Oakland Athletics to a 4-3 victory over the Baltimore Orioles on Saturday.

Myers (0-1) came in to start the ninth and retired the first two batters he faced. Damon Mashore doubled before Giambi hit an 0-1 pitch over the centerfield fence for his fourth home run of the season.
It was the first runs allowed this season by Myers, who blew his first save opportunity in 12 chances as Baltimore saw its four-game winning streak end.
"It was a big hit for Jason," said Oakland manager Art Howe. "The guy (Myers) doesn't give up too many home runs to lefthanders. It was a big lift for us."
Aaron Small (4-0) pitched 1 2/3 scoreless innings in relief of starter Mike Mohler for the victory.
Scott Spiezio hit a solo homer in the fifth and Brent Mayne doubled in a run for Oakland. Cal Ripken and Pete Incaviglia hit back-to-back homers in the sixth for Baltimore.

In Seattle, Matt Mieske had three hits, including a homer, John Jaha added a three-run shot and Tim Unroe cracked a grand slam as the Milwaukee Brewers tied a franchise record with 11 extra-base hits in a 17-4 rout of the Mariners.
Mieske had two doubles and a solo blast and Mike Matheny added a pair of doubles to pace the Brewers' 17-hit attack.
Bryce Florie (1-0) tossed 2 1/3 innings of effective relief to notch his first American League win.
Seattle's Jeff Fassero (4-1) was roughed up for seven runs and seven hits in just 1 2/3 innings.
The Mariners led 2-0 after the first inning, but Milwaukee exploded for eight runs in the second. Norm Charlton, the fifth Seattle pitcher, gave up five runs in the ninth.

In Toronto, a bases-loaded walk to Carlos Delgado with two out in the ninth scored Otis Nixon with the winning run as the Blue Jays blew a two-run lead in the top half of the inning before recovering for a 6-5 victory over the Minnesota Twins.
Todd Ritchie (2-3) took the loss, but it was Gregg Olson who walked Ed Sprague to load the bases before throwing four straight balls to Delgado, forcing home Nixon.
Paul Quantrill (4-2) got the win despite blowing a two-run lead in the top of the ninth.
In Cleveland, Sandy Alomar singled home pinch-runner Chad Curtis with the winning run to cap a two-run ninth inning as the Indians nipped the Detroit Tigers 7-6.
Since Cleveland moved into Jacobs Field, the Indians are 19-1 against the Tigers at home.
Doug Brocail (0-3) started the ninth for Detroit and took the loss. Eric Plunk (1-2) worked two innings for the win.
Cleveland tied the game, 6-6, when Matt Williams scored on a David Justice sacrifice fly.
Tony Clark had a three-run homer for Detroit in the third.
In Kansas City, Tim Belcher pitched a complete-game eight-hitter and Joe Vitiello had an RBI double in the sixth as the Royals edged the New York Yankees 2-1.

Belcher (3-3) allowed one run, walked two and struck out three for his 38th career complete game. Andy Pettitte (5-1) had his career-high five-game winning streak snapped, allowing two runs -- one earned -- and six hits through eight innings.
The Royals picked up their other run in the third on Jay Bell's RBI double.
In Chicago, the White Sox split a double header with the Anaheim Angels.
In the opener, Allen Watson pitched seven scoreless innings and Jack Howell and Garret Anderson had RBI doubles to give Anaheim a 3-2 victory.
Watson (1-2) scattered eight hits and walked one with three strikeouts for the win. James Baldwin (0-4) allowed two runs for the loss. He did not suffer his fourth loss last season until August 24.
In the second game, Doug Drabek allowed two hits over seven innings and Ray Durham had a double, homer and three RBI as the White Sox rebounded for a 4-2 win over the Angels.
Drabek (2-3) allowed only a homer to Jack Howell in the third and a single to Orlando Palmeiro in the sixth. He walked none and struck out six.
Durham hit his second homer in the third and added a two-run double in the fourth for the White Sox.
At Texas, Dean Palmer's two-run single with one out in the bottom of the ninth inning off closer Heathcliff Slocumb gave the Rangers a 7-6 win over the Boston Red Sox.
The Rangers won when trailing after eight innings for the first time in 106 games, dating back to June 28, 1995.
Ed Vosberg (1-1) struck out Darren Bragg with the bases loaded and two out in the top of the ninth to get the win.
Rudy Pemberton had four RBI, including a three-run homer in the fifth that gave the Red Sox a 6-4 lead.
